scenes.visual: Title card 'What Was Dated?' fades in over a schematic map of Africa and western Asia. COLOUR MAP, same in both films: TEAL = Homo sapiens (modern humans); ORANGE = Neanderthal; PURPLE = Denisovan; GREY-GOLD = ash and dated layers, flints and date tags. Cream background, 16:9. Every number appears only as on-screen text. Skulls, maps and chromosomes are simple labelled cartoons; anything not computed is labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: Did our species begin in one place, on one date? A skull from Jebel Irhoud, in Morocco, seems to answer yes. It comes with a date that looks precise.
scenes.visual: A grey-gold pin drops on Morocco labelled 'Jebel Irhoud'. A TEAL skull cartoon rises from the pin; a tag beside it reads '~315,000 years?' with a question mark that pulses.
scenes.narration: Did our species begin in one place, on one date? A skull from Jebel Irhoud, in Morocco, seems to answer yes. It comes with a date that looks precise.

scenes.tts: It has a face you could pass in the street. Its braincase is more elongated than yours. It is a mosaic of modern and older features.
scenes.visual: The skull rotates to side view. The face and teeth glow TEAL with label 'face, jaw, teeth: modern'. The braincase outline stretches longer and lower, shaded grey, labelled 'braincase: more primitive'. A banner: 'mosaic'.
scenes.narration: It has a face you could pass in the street. Its braincase is more elongated than yours. It is a mosaic of modern and older features.

scenes.tts: Now ask the question that runs through this whole lesson. What was actually dated? Not the skull itself. Flints lay beside the bones, and a fire had heated them.
scenes.visual: A cut-away of the ground opens under the pin like a drawer. Grey-gold flint chips lie beside the TEAL bones in one layer. The '~315,000' tag slides off the skull and sticks onto the flints.
scenes.narration: Now ask the question that runs through this whole lesson. What was actually dated? Not the skull itself. Flints lay beside the bones, and a fire had heated them.

scenes.tts: Enough heat resets the flint's signal. Afterward, radiation from the flint and its surroundings builds it back. The stored dose, divided by the yearly dose, gives the time since heating.
scenes.visual: A small flame flickers over one flint, then goes out; a counter on the flint resets to zero. Tiny grey-gold dots drift in from the surrounding sediment, a few glow from inside the flint, and a faint arrow comes down from above labelled 'cosmic rays'; they fill a gauge on the flint labelled 'dose stored'. On screen: 'dose stored / yearly dose = time since heating'. Then: '315,000 +/- 34,000 years (Richter et al., 2017)'.
scenes.narration: Enough heat resets the flint's signal. Afterward, radiation from the flint and its surroundings builds it back. The stored dose, divided by the yearly dose, gives the time since heating.

scenes.tts: So this date belongs to something beside the bones, not to the bones themselves. Every date in this story needs that same check.
scenes.visual: An arrow labelled 'dated' points at the flints; a second arrow labelled 'fossil' points at the skull. A checklist card appears: 'What was dated? Where did it lie?'
scenes.narration: So this date belongs to something beside the bones, not to the bones themselves. Every date in this story needs that same check.

scenes.tts: Travel east to Omo, in Ethiopia. Here a fossil lies in one layer, and a band of volcanic ash lies above it. The eruption that laid the ash has been dated too.
scenes.visual: A second pin drops on Ethiopia, 'Omo I'. Cut-away: a layer cake of sediment, a TEAL skull fragment in a middle band, a thin pale grey-gold ash band above it. A schematic volcano puffs ash that settles into that band. A date tag lands on the ash: '~233,000 years (eruption)'. Label 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Travel east to Omo, in Ethiopia. Here a fossil lies in one layer, and a band of volcanic ash lies above it. The eruption that laid the ash has been dated too.

scenes.tts: The ash lies above the bone, and the date belongs to the ash. So is the bone older or younger than that date?
scenes.visual: The layer cake holds still. An arrow from the ash's date tag points down at the skull, with two choices flashing: 'older?' 'younger?'
scenes.narration: The ash lies above the bone, and the date belongs to the ash. So is the bone older or younger than that date?

scenes.visual: Hold on the layer cake with the two choices; a small timer ring fills over five seconds.

scenes.tts: At least as old. The ash fell after the bone was buried. So its date is a minimum. Omo One is at least about that old, not dated directly.
scenes.caption: At least as old. The ash fell after the bone was buried. So its date is a minimum. Omo I is at least about that old, not dated directly.
scenes.visual: Rewind animation: the bone settles first and is covered with sediment, then the ash falls on top. The skull's tag now reads 'at least ~233,000 years (minimum)'. 'older?' turns TEAL with a tick.
scenes.narration: At least as old. The ash fell after the bone was buried. So its date is a minimum. Omo I is at least about that old, not dated directly.

scenes.tts: Now cross into western Asia. At Misliya Cave, in Israel, a jaw with teeth from our lineage turned up. It was dated far earlier than the dispersal many textbooks taught. Part of that dating has been challenged.
scenes.visual: A third pin drops on Israel, 'Misliya Cave'. A TEAL upper jaw with teeth appears. On screen: '177,000-194,000 years ago (part of the dating challenged)' and, struck through faintly, 'textbook dispersal ~60,000 years ago'.
scenes.narration: Now cross into western Asia. At Misliya Cave, in Israel, a jaw with teeth from our lineage turned up. It was dated far earlier than the dispersal many textbooks taught. Part of that dating has been challenged.

scenes.tts: Does that mean living people outside Africa descend from them? Not by itself. A fossil shows presence, not ancestry. Genomes of living non-Africans point mainly to a later dispersal.
scenes.visual: A thin TEAL thread runs from Africa to the Misliya pin and fades out. A thicker TEAL thread leaves Africa later on the time bar and continues on, labelled 'later dispersal (genomes)'. Card: 'presence is not ancestry'.
scenes.narration: Does that mean living people outside Africa descend from them? Not by itself. A fossil shows presence, not ancestry. Genomes of living non-Africans point mainly to a later dispersal.

scenes.tts: So the dates do not mark one birthplace. People with partly modern anatomy lived in north Africa very early. They lived in east Africa by at least the Omo date.
scenes.visual: A time bar slides in under the map. Each date tag drops onto it with a small grey-gold label of what was dated: 'heated flints, beside' (Jebel Irhoud), 'ash, above: minimum' (Omo I), 'jaw, partly challenged' (Misliya). On screen: 'north Africa: ~300,000 years ago' and 'east Africa: by at least ~233,000 years ago'.
scenes.narration: So the dates do not mark one birthplace. People with partly modern anatomy lived in north Africa very early. They lived in east Africa by at least the Omo date.

scenes.tts: Genomes of living people agree that most of our ancestry traces to Africa. But the history is not one tree with one root. It is connected populations that split, and sometimes merged again.
scenes.visual: A single tree with one root labelled 'one place, one date' dissolves. In its place a braided stream of TEAL channels flows across a schematic Africa: channels split apart and rejoin. Label 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Genomes of living people agree that most of our ancestry traces to Africa. But the history is not one tree with one root. It is connected populations that split, and sometimes merged again.

scenes.tts: So whenever you meet a date in this story, ask two plain questions before you believe it. What was dated? And where did it lie?
scenes.visual: The checklist card from earlier returns large, centred: 'What was dated? Where did it lie?' The three pins glow one after another.
scenes.narration: So whenever you meet a date in this story, ask two plain questions before you believe it. What was dated? And where did it lie?

scenes.visual: Hex end card. Line: 'Ask what was dated, and where it lay.'
